drivingQuestion: Whose opinion does Rav Huna follow when he says the hide nullifies two attached half olive-bulks, and what does his ruling add?
outcomeNote: The first explanation (that R' Yishmael's denial covers only an animal-torn hide) is defeated by the alal mishna; Rav Huna is finally set with R' Akiva, and his ruling is shown to add that R' Akiva's reason applies to a hide torn by an animal no less than one flayed by a knife.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים שֶׁיֶּשְׁנָן עַל גַּבֵּי הָעוֹר – הָעוֹר מְבַטְּלָן,
segments.en: «And Rav Huna says:» In a case of «two» pieces of flesh of an animal carcass, each measuring «half an olive-»bulk, «that are» attached «to the hide, the hide nullifies them,» as the hide does not impart the impurity of a carcass. Consequently, these pieces do not impart impurity either.

The Gemara asks: «In accordance with whose» opinion is the statement of Rav Huna? It is taught in the mishna (124a) that in a case where the hide of an unslaughtered carcass was attached to two half olive-bulks of flesh, Rabbi Yishmael says that the hide imparts the impurity of an unslaughtered carcass by means of carrying but not by means of contact with the flesh, because one touches them separately whereas one carries them together. Rabbi Akiva says: One contracts impurity neither by means of contact with the hide nor by means of carrying it.

segments.he: אִי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל – הָאָמַר לֹא מְבַטֵּל עוֹר. וְאִי אַלִּיבָּא דְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – פְּשִׁיטָא, הָאָמַר מְבַטֵּל עוֹר.
segments.en: «If» one maintains that Rav Huna’s statement is «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Yishmael, didn’t» Rabbi Yishmael «say» that the «hide does not nullify» the attached flesh and therefore the one who carries it becomes impure with the impurity of a carcass? «And if» one maintains that Rav Huna’s statement is «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Akiva,» then it is «obvious,» as «didn’t» Rabbi Akiva «say» that «the hide nullifies» the flesh and therefore one who carries it does not become impure?

segments.he: לְעוֹלָם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וְכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא מְבַטֵּל עוֹר – הָנֵי מִילֵּי שֶׁפְּלָטַתּוּ חָיָה, אֲבָל פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין – בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Actually,» the statement of Rav Huna is «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Yishmael. And when Rabbi Yishmael said» that «the hide does not nullify» the flesh, «that statement» applies to a case «where an animal severed» the hide. «But» in a case where a person used «a knife» to «flay» the hide, the hide «nullifies» the attached flesh.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הָאָלָל הַמְכוּנָּס, אִם יֵשׁ כְּזַיִת בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד – חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו, וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְהוּא שֶׁכִּנְּסוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» a refutation to this explanation of the statement of Rav Huna from that which is taught in the mishna: «Rabbi Yehuda says:» With regard to «the meat residue» attached to the hide after flaying «that was collected, if there is an olive-bulk» of it «in one place» it imparts impurity of an animal carcass, and one who contracts impurity from it and eats consecrated foods or enters the Temple «is liable» to receive karet «for it. And Rav Huna says» in explanation of this statement of Rabbi Yehuda: This halakha «is» applicable only when a halakhically competent person «collected» the meat residue in one place, but not if the meat residue was collected by a child or without human intervention.

segments.he: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין, לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל נָמֵי לָא בָּטֵיל, רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
segments.en: Since Rav Huna interprets the statement of Rabbi Yehuda as referring to a case where a halakhically competent person collected the pieces of flesh, the mishna must be discussing a case where such a person flayed the hide with a knife in multiple places and then collected the pieces of flesh attached to the hide. Evidently, the hide does not nullify the flesh because if the hide did nullify the flesh, that flesh would not impart the impurity of a carcass even if it were later collected. Therefore, the Gemara challenges: «Granted, if you say» that «according to Rabbi Yishmael, even» in a case where a person used «a knife» to «flay» the hide, the hide «does not nullify» the flesh, accordingly, «Rav Huna said» his statement «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yishmael» that a hide flayed by a knife does not nullify the flesh, and therefore the flesh imparts the impurity of a carcass if a person collected the pieces.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין, לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בָּטֵיל, רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּמַאן?
segments.en: «But if you say» that «according to Rabbi Yishmael,» in a case where a person used «a knife» to «flay» the hide, the hide «nullifies» the flesh and therefore the flesh does not impart the impurity of a carcass even if a halakhically competent person collected the pieces, then «in accordance with whose» opinion «did Rav Huna say» that the hide does not nullify the flesh and that the pieces of flesh that one collected impart the impurity of a carcass?

segments.he: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין, לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לֹא בָּטֵיל, וְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא!
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Rather,» it is necessary to explain the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael differently. «Actually, according to Rabbi Yishmael» even a hide «flayed by a knife does not nullify» the attached flesh. «And Rav Huna said» his statement that the hide nullifies attached pieces of flesh «in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Akiva.»

segments.he: פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא – הָנֵי מִילֵּי פְּלָטַתּוּ סַכִּין, אֲבָל פְּלָטַתּוּ חַיָּה – לָא בָּטֵיל.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: Isn’t it «obvious» that the hide nullifies the flesh according to Rabbi Akiva? Rav Huna’s statement is unnecessary. The Gemara answers: Rav Huna’s statement is necessary «lest you say: When Rabbi Akiva said» that the hide nullifies the attached pieces of flesh, «that statement» applies only to a case where a person used «a knife» to «flay» the animal. «But» if «an animal severed» the hide, the hide «does not nullify» the flesh.

segments.he: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָעוֹר מְבַטְּלָן, לָא שְׁנָא (פלט) [פְּלָטַתּוּ] חַיָּה, וְלָא שְׁנָא (פלט) [פְּלָטַתּוּ] סַכִּין, כִּדְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְטַהֵר בְּעוֹר? מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָעוֹר מְבַטְּלָן.
segments.en: Therefore, Rav Huna «teaches us» that «the reason» for the opinion «of Rabbi Akiva» is «because the hide nullifies» the flesh, and there «is no difference» whether «an animal severed» the hide, «and» there «is no difference» whether a person used «a knife» to «flay» the hide. This statement of Rav Huna is therefore «in accordance with that which the latter clause» of that mishna «teaches: For what» reason «does Rabbi Akiva deem» one ritually «pure in» a case where he moved both half olive-bulks with «the hide?» It is «because the hide» separates between them and «nullifies them.»

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב הונא: שני חצאי זיתים שישנן על גבי העור
moves.summary: a second ruling of Rav Huna, joined by ו to his gloss on the alal clause in the preceding unit: the hide nullifies two attached half olive-bulks
moves.about: Rav Huna's further ruling that a hide nullifies two attached half olive-bulks of carcass flesh

moves.summary: whose opinion does Rav Huna's ruling follow?
moves.about: which of the tannaim of the mishna on hides Rav Huna's ruling follows

moves.cueHe: אי אליבא דרבי ישמעאל – האמר לא מבטל עור
moves.summary: the first candidate is knocked down: R' Yishmael holds the hide does not nullify
moves.about: the floated identification of Rav Huna with R' Yishmael, who holds the opposite of what Rav Huna said

moves.summary: the second candidate is knocked down as superfluous: R' Akiva already says the hide nullifies
moves.about: on the other horn, that Rav Huna follows R' Akiva, his ruling is superfluous since R' Akiva already said the hide nullifies

moves.summary: Rav Huna does follow R' Yishmael, whose denial of nullification covers only a hide torn off by an animal, not one flayed with a knife
moves.about: Rav Huna does follow R' Yishmael, whose denial of nullification is limited to a hide torn off by an animal

moves.cueHe: תא שמע, רבי יהודה אומר: האלל המכונס
moves.summary: the mishna on collected alal, with Rav Huna's own gloss on it, is brought against that explanation
moves.about: the mishna's clause on R' Yehuda and collected meat residue, with Rav Huna's gloss on it

moves.summary: granted horn: if a knife-flayed hide does not nullify for R' Yishmael, Rav Huna's alal gloss follows R' Yishmael
moves.about: whether R' Yishmael can be said to hold that a knife-flayed hide nullifies the flesh, given that Rav Huna lets collected residue impart impurity

moves.cueHe: אלא אי אמרת פלטתו סכין, לרבי ישמעאל בטיל
moves.summary: but on the explanation just given, whose opinion could Rav Huna's alal gloss follow?
moves.about: whose view Rav Huna's alal gloss could follow if a knife-flayed hide nullifies for R' Yishmael too

moves.cueHe: אלא לעולם פלטתו סכין, לרבי ישמעאל לא בטיל
moves.summary: the limitation is withdrawn: for R' Yishmael a knife-flayed hide too does not nullify, and Rav Huna follows R' Akiva
moves.about: retracting the limitation: for R' Yishmael even a knife-flayed hide does not nullify, and Rav Huna follows R' Akiva

moves.summary: then Rav Huna merely restates R' Akiva and teaches nothing
moves.about: if Rav Huna merely restates R' Akiva, his ruling teaches nothing

moves.summary: floats the supposition that R' Akiva's nullification holds only for a knife-flayed hide, which Rav Huna comes to exclude
moves.about: Rav Huna is needed to exclude the supposition that R' Akiva's nullification applies only to a knife-flayed hide

moves.cueHe: קא משמע לן טעמא דרבי עקיבא מפני שהעור מבטלן
moves.summary: Rav Huna teaches that R' Akiva's reason is the hide's nullifying, so animal-torn and knife-flayed are alike
moves.about: R' Akiva's reason is that the hide nullifies, so it makes no difference whether an animal tore it or a knife flayed it
